title: LiquidPanc: Liquid Biopsy Integrated Quantification and Detection Platform for Pancreatic Cancer
summary:
Pancreatic cancer is a serious disease whose course is often difficult to assess despite surgery and chemotherapy. Imaging methods (computed tomography, MRI) and the tumor marker CA 19-9 in the blood are the established tools for monitoring disease, but they have limits in their sensitivity. In recent years, the so-called liquid biopsy has come to the forefront of research as a complementary approach. In a liquid biopsy, fragments of tumor genetic material released into the blood are detected from a simple blood draw. In pancreatic cancer, however, the concentration of these tumor genetic fragments in the blood is particularly low, so conventional methods often do not suffice to reliably detect them.

The main aim of this study is therefore to establish a multi-platform analytical pipeline for the detection and quantification of tumor genetic material in the blood of patients with non-metastatic pancreatic cancer. Two complementary genetic-testing techniques are combined to substantially increase the sensitivity of the liquid biopsy. On this basis, it will be investigated whether disease course can in the future be more accurately captured and monitored. The study enrolls 60 patients with non-metastatic pancreatic cancer across three disease stages, together with 20 individuals without cancer as a comparison group. The findings should help to monitor future patients with pancreatic cancer more accurately and to tailor treatment more individually.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed PDAC; non-metastatic disease (locally advanced, borderline resectable, or resectable); planned induction/neoadjuvant chemotherapy or planned surgical resection; age ≥ 18 years; ability to understand character and individual consequences of the trial; written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Inability to understand consequences or comply with study; participation in another interventional trial with interference of intervention and outcome of this study; any condition which could result in an undue risk for the patient in the opinion of the investigator
